npcs.notes:
**Character & Alignment:** Deckard Cain (`character_cain_the_storyteller`. Town Elder of Tristram and last of the Horadrim. Lawful good, weighted toward grim duty.)

**Abilities, Spells or Mechanics:**
Cain does not fight. He identifies unidentified magical items, advises on their hidden capabilities, and carries the Horadrim's lore on Diablo, Mephisto, Baal, and the Soulstones. His real power is knowledge: he can name a demon, a ritual, or a relic, and he knows the cost of each.

**Want / Need / Wound:**
*Want:* to keep Tristram alive and to find a hero who can finish what the Horadrim began. *Need:* to stop being the last witness and trust someone else with the burden. *Wound:* he is the last of an order that gave its life to seal the Three, and he has watched the seal fail.

**Voice & Sensory Tells:**
Slow, warm, stagey, a storyteller's cadence that gives way to dread. "Stay awhile and listen." His tells are a hand to his beard before a hard truth, and the way his voice drops when he names Diablo. As the corruption spreads he stops finishing the sentences that frighten him.

**Secrets & Leverage:**
He knows the Soulstone can bind but not destroy, and that a living host is a failing prison. He has never said how many Horadrim he watched die. His vulnerability is the town: threaten Tristram and he will give up anything.

**Crucible Reaction:**
He pushes the hero toward understanding before force. At the Mad King's tomb he tells the full story of the lost prince. At the Soulstone he argues for binding by ritual, not for the forehead. If the hero hosts Diablo, Cain stays beside them as long as he is able and records everything.

### Deepened Dossier
*Uldyssian's echo:* wants the hero to see that absorbing a cosmos costs the self. *Rathma's echo:* wants the hero to see that destroying evil only moves it. *Wound (shared):* both know what happens to mortals who try.

The Soulstone is a splinter of the Worldstone, and it remembers. *Tragic leverage:* they can offer the hero the truth about what hosting does, and the hero cannot un-know it.

They do not intervene. At the Soulstone they speak once each: Uldyssian warns against becoming the vessel; Rathma warns against shattering it. Neither will say which choice is right, because neither knows.

### Deepened Dossier
*Want:* to bring the Lord of Terror a vessel and be spared. *Need:* absolution he has made impossible to grant. *Wound:* he betrayed his king and led a rescue party into a trap, and every day since has been spent proving to himself that it was necessary.

The grimoire is his weakness and his weapon. He has told himself Albrecht's suffering is a price to pay. *Tragic leverage:* he is a coward who believes he is a martyr. A hero who can offer him real confession, with real consequences, can make him falter at the ritual's last line.

If the hero knows his name from Farnham and Cain, he treats the hero as a rival priest. If not, he treats them as a sacrament. He dies still preaching.

quests.notes:
**Milestone & Crucible:** Milestone 1: The Cleaver and the Dying Man (Milestone 1, `cr_01_01` (src: The Cleaver Corrupts))

**Dungeon Tier & Phase:** Dungeon Level 2, Zone I: The Cathedral (`ph_01`, Arrival and the Butcher)

**Canonical Outcome:**
The hero hears the dying townsman's plea at the church door, lures the Butcher behind a grated door, kills him with arrows, and takes the Cleaver. Soon after, the hero trades it for a weapon that suits their class. The slaughter ends, and the descent continues. Every kill brings Aidan one step closer to the corruption that makes him the Dark Wanderer.

**Crucible Divergence Point:**
Keep the Cleaver, or put it down. The Cleaver kills most things in a single swipe for a few levels, and it is also a demon's tool. Keeping it is the efficient, brutal choice. Surrendering it to Griswold's forge, or leaving it on the Butcher's corpse, costs the hero their edge. A second fork sits underneath: kill the Butcher by the clean grating trick, or let him into open melee and learn what his hunger feels like.

**Immediate Dilemma and Cost:**
The Cleaver's power is real and the hero needs it. Wielding it draws watching eyes in the dark, and the townsfolk see a butcher's blade on a stranger's belt. Pepin flinches at the hero's wounds. Griswold will not repair it. The cost is trust, plus a creeping sense that the weapon is choosing the strokes.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
A hero who keeps the Cleaver walks into every later fight already marked as one of the Butcher's kind. Lazarus's whispers find easy purchase on a hero who has already taken a demon's weapon. Tristram's last survivors will remember the hero as a second slaughterer, not a savior. By the time Diablo II opens, the wanderer on the road is the sort of figure that villagers cross themselves to see.

**Crucible Divergence Point:**
Take Adria seriously, or ignore her. If the hero reads the stolen sign, the fouled spring, the dark riders and the dying man's tale as one design, they can hunt the hand behind it (Lazarus) before descending further. If they don't, they keep fighting symptoms. The hero must also decide how far to trust Adria, whose shop sells the Town Portals and mana that keep them alive and whose motives are nobody's idea of simple.

**Immediate Dilemma and Cost:**
Pausing to investigate costs time while the town goes thirsty and Pepin's stocks dwindle. Questioning Adria costs her goodwill, and she is the only source of mana potions and Town Portals. Acting on the pattern means committing to a theory with no proof.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
A hero who reads the pattern arrives in Hell already knowing Lazarus's name and his purpose. That changes the Hell-tier fork (Milestone 9) from a surprise into a choice. A hero who ignores the pattern meets Lazarus as a revelation, too late to save Albrecht. Either way, Adria's trust shapes whether she will answer the hard questions about the Soulstone, and whether she tells the truth about what she has been waiting for.

What the hero learned from the tomes shapes how well they understand Lazarus's grimoire in Hell. **Dungeon Tier & Phase:** Dungeon Levels 13 to 15, Zone IV: Hell

**Canonical Outcome:**
The hero kills the Warlord of Blood and reaches Archbishop Lazarus at his Unholy Altar. Lazarus has kidnapped Prince Albrecht, the Archbishop's own king's son and Leoric's lost child, and used the boy as a sacrifice to Diablo. The hero cannot save him. **Crucible Divergence Point:**
Burn Lazarus's grimoire, or read it. The Warlord of Blood's gauntlet is a tactical test of the hero's party and resources. Lazarus's ritual book is a moral one. Burning it denies every future summoner the incantation. Reading it gives the hero the knowledge to interrupt the sacrifice, bind Diablo's vessel, or even speak the old words. A third fork is Albrecht himself: strike at the boy to end the vessel, or try to carry him out alive.

**Immediate Dilemma and Cost:**
Reading the grimoire costs sanity, and a fragment of the hero's will goes into every syllable. Burning it costs the one weapon that could unmake the sacrifice. Sparing Albrecht costs time against a ritual already underway, and killing him costs a child's life and the last of Leoric's line.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
A hero who reads the book carries Lazarus's words into Diablo's chamber and into Diablo II, where the Dark Wanderer is a scholar of the very ritual that damned him. A hero who burns it leaves Hell's mouth a little more closed, and the next summoner of demons has to start from nothing. Albrecht's fate is the tragedy's hinge: a boy who survives as a ruined vessel is the seed of a different Wanderer, and a boy who dies leaves Diablo free to find a more willing host.

This campaign uses the retcon as its tragic spine.* The hero kills Diablo, the Lord of Terror, in his sanctum. The Soulstone that held Diablo's essence falls free. The hero, driven by the belief that his own body can contain it, drives the shard into his own forehead. Prince Aidan, the hero, becomes the Dark Wanderer: a man hollowed by the demon he has taken in. Diablo II begins with the Wanderer on the road to Tristram's ruins.

**Crucible Divergence Point:**
Drive the shard into one's own forehead, or choose another way. The hero can contain Diablo in their own flesh (canon), carry the Soulstone to Cain and the Horadrim's last scholars for a ritual of binding, leave it for Adria, who wants it, or shatter it and release the essence to Hell. Hosting Diablo costs the hero everything: mind, name, and the slow certainty that the demon will take the wheel. Carrying the stone to Cain costs time that Diablo's brothers will use. **Dungeon Tier & Phase:** Dungeon Level 14 (Lachdanan's chamber) and Dungeon Level 15 (where the Golden Elixir is found), Zone IV: Hell. *Source note: the walkthrough places the elixir on Level 15 and the quest-giver on Level 14, so the choice spans two floors.*

**Canonical Outcome:**
General Lachdanan, cursed captain of Leoric's Royal Guard, asks the hero to find a golden elixir that will lift his curse. The hero brings it. Lachdanan thanks them, gives up the Veil of Steel, and his body is gone. The hero walks on with a helm and a lighter dungeon.

**Crucible Divergence Point:**
Free him, kill him, or use him. Lachdanan knows Hell's royal armory and Lazarus's side passages, and as long as he stays cursed he can guide the hero through them.
- **Tactical fork 1, Deliver the elixir at once.** He dies content, the Veil is yours, and his knowledge dies with him unless the hero asked first.
- **Tactical fork 2, Withhold the elixir until he has shown the way.** The hero gets his route through Level 15 and a safer approach to the red portal. Each hour he waits, the curse presses harder on him, and a general who has begged once will not beg twice.
- **Tactical fork 3, Drink the elixir.** The hero keeps the draught for themselves. It is not made for the living, and the hero finds out why.
- **Tactical fork 4, Cut him down.** His death by the hero's hand is violence against a man who asked for mercy, and it forfeits the Veil.

**Immediate Dilemma and Cost:**
Time and conscience. Bargaining with a dying knight costs the hero his own sense of being the hero. The cursed guard under his command (Blood Knights and the remnant of the Royal Guard) respond to his state, and a Lachdanan who feels betrayed turns his men against the hero. *Irreversible costs:* once freed he cannot be brought back, so his testimony about Leoric's last words is sealed. Once denied, he cannot be freed by anyone else, since there is only one elixir.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
A freed Lachdanan leaves the Royal Guard leaderless, and the Blood Knights below turn feral. A hero who kept him alive learns the armory's layout, which makes the Level 15 ritual (Milestone 12) survivable, and also learns what Leoric said as he died, which shades how the hero judges Lazarus. A hero who killed him gives Hell its first story about the human who murders the suppliant. In Diablo II the Wanderer's reputation, in the villages he passes, is built from tales like this one.

The hero takes Lazarus' Staff to Cain, learns what it opens, and enters the red portal on Level 15. In the lair, grey circles and books teleport the hero between rooms. quests.notes:
**Milestone & Crucible:** Milestone 13: The Soulstone Dilemma (Deepened) (Milestone 13, `cr_hell_soulstone_dilemma_deep` (authored; deepens Milestone 10, `cr_hell_soulstone_choice`))

**Dungeon Tier & Phase:** Dungeon Level 16, Zone IV: Hell (Diablo's sanctum)

**Canonical Outcome:**
Diablo falls. In the original game Albrecht's body is left on the floor, the stone cracked from his forehead, a dead boy. In the retcon the hero kneels, picks up the shard and drives it into their own forehead, believing flesh can hold what the Horadrim's stone could not. Later stories name that hero Aidan, and the man who walks east in Diablo II is the Dark Wanderer.

**Crucible Divergence Point:**
Five choices, each with an advocate in the room and a price paid on the spot.
- **Fork A, Take it into the forehead.** Advocate: the Soulstone itself, which sounds exactly like the hero's own exhaustion. Cost: the hero's name, slowly, and the certainty that Diablo is awake behind the eyes.
- **Fork B, Carry it to Cain.** Advocate: Cain, if the hero kept him alive and informed. Cost: a journey back up through sixteen levels with Diablo's essence loose in the shard, and every demon that notices.
- **Fork C, Give it to Adria.** Advocate: Adria, who has wanted it all along. Cost: trust, and the knowledge that she will use it.
- **Fork D, Shatter it.** Advocate: the voice of Rathma, if the hero has heard it (see his dossier). Cost: the essence is released into the world instead of contained.
- **Fork E, Leave it with Albrecht's body.** Advocate: nobody. Cost: the next person through the labyrinth finds a child and a stone.

**Immediate Dilemma and Cost:**
The hero is wounded, out of supplies and alone. Any choice other than A means walking out with the stone, and the stone does not stay quiet. *Irreversible costs:* every choice here is permanent. The hero cannot unswallow the shard, cannot reassemble a shattered one, cannot recover a stone left behind once the sanctum collapses.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
This is the hinge that Diablo II hangs from. A hero who hosts Diablo becomes the Wanderer, and the war in Khanduras arrives with Mephisto and Baal behind it. A hero who delivered the stone to Cain gives the Horadrim one more chance to repeat the lesson of Tal Rasha, which is that a living prison fails. A hero who gave it to Adria arms a rival with a Prime Evil's heart. A hero who shattered it breaks the stone and frees the essence to find a new host. The echo of Uldyssian is the unspoken comparison: he absorbed a cosmos in his own body and was erased for it. The hero who takes the stone is walking the same road, with fewer gods watching.
---

**Dungeon Tier & Phase:** Dungeon Descent

**Canonical Outcome:**
The heroes triumph through grim sacrifice.

**Crucible Divergence Point:**
Trust Lilith's whispers or heed Mendeln and the Dragon's caution. Uldyssian can embrace the intoxicating power of his awakened godhood to slaughter his accusers instantly, or seek the cosmic balance taught by Rathma and Trag'Oul.
- **Immediate Dilemma & Cost:** Embracing raw Nephalem wrath incinerates entire temples effortlessly, but warps the Edyrem into ruthless tyrants who mirror the demons they fight. Seeking the Balance requires sparing enemies who seek to burn them at the stake.

**Immediate Dilemma and Cost:**
High cost in blood and spiritual purity.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Altering Uldyssian's path determines whether humanity's Nephalem power remains completely forgotten after the Worldstone's wipe, or whether secret bloodlines retain their active heritage into the Tristram crisis.

- **Immediate Dilemma & Cost:** Self-sacrifice erases Uldyssian and resets mortal civilization to fragile ignorance. Conquering Heaven and Hell locks Sanctuary into eternal, apocalyptic total war against both celestial legions and endless demonic hordes.

High cost in blood and spiritual purity.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
If Uldyssian chose conquest, Tristram is not a sleepy hamlet in a fallen kingdom, but a heavily fortified arcane bastion of god-emperors.

The purity and resolve of the Horadrim are forged here. If Tal Rasha was saved, the Horadric brotherhood never degenerated into forgotten hermit-scholars like Deckard Cain, but remained an active standing army of magi in Khanduras.

items.name: The Red Soulstone of Terror
items.specs: Prime Horadric binding crystal containing the essence of Diablo, burning with infernal will.
items.notes: A jagged crimson crystal shard pulsating with an ominous internal heartbeat, forged by the Archangel Tyrael to bind the Lord of Terror. Discovered lodged within the skull of Prince Albrecht within the burning Pentagram Sanctum on Hell Level 16. It radiates unbearable psychic heat and whispers ancient demonic blasphemies into the bearer's mind, tempting them with absolute dominion in exchange for driving the crystal into their own forehead.

items.name: The Butcher's Cleaver
items.specs: Heavy jagged meat-hook cleaver dealing savage crushing wounds (Damage: 4-24, +10 Strength).
items.notes: A colossal, notched iron meat cleaver encrusted with coagulated human gore and demonic grease, wielded by the demon Butcher in his charnel room on Level 2 of the Cathedral. The weapon carries immense heft and brutal cleaving power, but exudes a nauseating slaughterhouse reek that makes nearby townsfolk and holy clergy flinch in revulsion.

items.name: Undead Crown of King Leoric
items.specs: Undead Royal Coronet (Armor Rating: 8, Life Steal: 3-6%, -100 Armor vs Lightning).
items.notes: The blackened, jewel-encrusted silver crown of Khanduras, worn by the reanimated King Leoric in his desecrated subterranean tomb beneath the Cathedral. The crown confers unholy life-leeching necromantic vitality upon the wearer, but resonates with Leoric's weeping madness and grief over his murdered son, steadily eroding the bearer's psychological composure.

items.name: Staff of Archbishop Lazarus
items.specs: Corrupted Archbishops Staff (Base Damage: 8-16, Fast Cast, Charged with Fireball).
items.notes: An ornate ceremonial staff of carved mammoth ivory, stained with dried blood and profane sigils of the Triune. Archbishop Lazarus leaned upon this staff when he deceitfully marched the armed townsfolk of Tristram into the labyrinth beneath the Cathedral, sealing the iron gates behind them to be butchered in the dark. It crackles with malevolent sorcery at the Unholy Altar.

items.name: The Veil of Steel
items.specs: Masterwork Greathelm (+18 Armor, +50% All Elemental Resistances, -20 Light Radius).
items.notes: A heavy, visorless Khanduras battle-helm worn by General Lachdanan during his tragic defense of the realm against King Leoric's descent into madness. While cursed along with the rest of Leoric's royal guard, Lachdanan retained a shred of honor. The helm renders the wearer virtually impervious to fire, frost, and lightning, though it shrouds their peripheral vision in perpetual gloom.

items.name: Pepin's Golden Elixir of Cleansing
items.specs: Sacred Cleansing Draught (Dispels Undead Curses, Restores Sanctity).
items.notes: A luminous, amber-colored alchemical philter concocted by Pepin the Healer using purified spring water from the cleansed Cathedral caverns and sacred mountain herbs. Specifically formulated to break King Leoric's blood curse on Lachdanan, allowing the condemned knight to die with his honor and soul intact.

items.name: Wirt's Peg Leg & Hidden Stash Map
items.specs: Hollowed Peg Leg (Contains Secret Smuggling Compartment and Map Shards).
items.notes: A hollowed wooden prosthetic leg worn by Wirt, the cynical young merchant boy of Tristram. Replaced after demons tore off his original leg when the Cathedral fell, the hollow interior serves as Wirt's private vault where he stashes black-market stolen goods, high-interest extortion IOUs, and cryptic maps pointing toward mythical secret realms.

items.name: Griswold's Edge Broadsword
items.specs: Broadsword (Damage: 12-28, Fire Damage: 1-10, +25 to Attack Rating, Fast Attack).
items.notes: A masterwork serrated broadsword forged by Griswold on his Tristram anvil from a fallen celestial skystone. The tempered steel glows cherry-red along its fuller, releasing bursts of incinerating flame with every strike. Griswold considers it the crowning achievement of his mortal blacksmithing career.

items.name: The Empyrean Band
items.specs: Horadric Platinum Signet (+2 to All Attributes, Light Radius +2, Fast Hit Recovery).
items.notes: An ancient Horadric platinum ring engraved with celestial geometric constellations, prized as an heirloom by Ogden of the Rising Sun Tavern. The ring fell into the hands of Snotspill's goblin raiders when they ransacked the tavern, but its latent warding magic repels demonic spiritual corruption.

items.name: The Rising Sun Tavern Sign
items.specs: Hand-Carved Oak Signboard (Heavy Blunt Relic, Morale Symbol).
items.notes: A weather-beaten wooden tavern sign featuring a cheerfully carved smiling sun, stolen from Ogden's inn by Snotspill's gang of Fallen Ones on Level 4 of the Cathedral. To the demons, it is a grand war trophy mocking humanity; to the frightened survivors shivering in Tristram, its return represents the faint promise of civilization enduring.

items.name: The Celestial Skystone (Magic Rock)
items.specs: Celestial Meteor Skystone (Pulsing Mana Conduit, Crafting Core).
items.notes: A heavy extraterrestrial aerolite recovered from Level 4 of the labyrinth, humming with raw celestial magicka and emitting cold blue luminescence. Coveted by Griswold to temper enchanted armor, the stone feels icy to the touch regardless of surrounding heat.

items.name: Arkaine's Valor Horadric Splint Mail
items.specs: Ancient Horadric Splint Mail (Armor: 25, Fast Hit Recovery, +10 Vitality, -3 Damage Taken).
items.notes: The sacred splint mail of Arkaine, legendary champion of the Horadrim who fell holding the catacomb breach during the Sin War. Interred within a warded crypt on Level 5, the breastplate is impervious to rust, miraculously deflecting demonic claws and absorbing kinetic shock.

items.name: The Mythic Folio of the Blind
items.specs: Horadric Mythic Codex (Illusion Mastery, Grants Infravision and Shadow Veil).
items.notes: A velvet-bound codex written in raised braille-like glyphs by the ancient blind order of Khanduras seers. Found upon a stone lectern within the darkened Hall of the Blind on Level 7, reading its poetic verses grants the ability to pierce subterranean gloom while muffling the party's footsteps.

items.name: The Book of Blood
items.specs: Ritual Grimoire (Unlocks the Blood Pedestal in the Chamber of Bone).
items.notes: A crimson-bound ceremonial tome resting in the bone-strewn corridors of the Catacombs. It recounts the blood-oath binding the Guardian of Khanduras and details the exact incantation required to activate the crimson font that unlocks the Chamber of Bone.

items.name: The Anvil of Fury
items.specs: Demonic Hellfire Anvil (Smelts Infernal Ores, Weight: 500 lbs).
items.notes: A gargantuan anvil carved from subterranean obsidian, burning with inextinguishable hellfire on Level 10 of the Magma Caverns. Left behind by demonic armorer Overlords, Griswold can use it to smelt celestial metals into gear capable of piercing Diablo's skin.

items.name: The Fungal Spore of the Magma Caverns
items.specs: Bioluminescent Cavern Fungi (Alchemical Catalyst of Supernatural Perception).
items.notes: A spongy, pitch-black fungal cluster dripping with luminescent spores, gathered from the humid geothermal vents of Caves Level 9. Required by Adria the Witch to brew the Spectral Elixir of True Sight, allowing mortals to perceive demonic astral anchors.

items.name: Shadowfang Cursed Longsword
items.specs: Cursed Longsword (Damage: 20-35, 10% Life Stolen per Hit, Curses Wielder's Vitality).
items.notes: A serrated black-steel longsword wielded by the Warlord of Blood on Hell Level 13. The blade feeds on spilled blood, repairing its own edge while transferring life force to its master, but gradually drains the moral conscience and warmth of anyone who holds it.

items.name: Harlequin Crest Shako
items.specs: Horadric Shako (+2 All Skills, +141 Life, +141 Mana, 10% Physical Damage Reduction).
items.notes: A court jester's enchanted cap crafted by eccentric Horadric scholars in mockery of the Lords of Hell. Hidden deep within the crypt vaults, its multicolored cloth weaves protective wards that absorb crushing blows while invigorating the mind.

items.name: Windforce Hydra Bow
items.specs: Hydra Bow (Damage: 35-50, Tremendous Knockback, +5 Dexterity, 20% Increased Attack Speed).
items.notes: A legendary recurve bow carved from fossilized wood and strung with woven hurricane winds. Found within the deepest magma caverns, every arrow released from its string strikes with the kinetic force of a gale, hurling demons backwards across corridors.

items.name: The Grandfather Colossus Blade
items.specs: Colossus Blade (Damage: 50-120, +20 All Attributes, +70% Life, Indestructible).
items.notes: A titanic two-handed broadsword of ancient craftsmanship, revered as the patriarchal blade of Khanduran chivalry. Sunk into an iron pedestal on Hell Level 14, its edge never chips or dulls, cleaving through armored demon warlords in a single thunderous arc.

items.name: Godly Plate of the Whale
items.specs: Godly Full Plate of the Whale (Armor: 200, +100 Life, -100% Enemy Critical Strike Chance).
items.notes: The undisputed pinnacle of heavy plate armor in Sanctuary, forged with shimmering white steel that reflects hellish glare. Recovered from the demon lords guarding Diablo's chamber, it renders the champion nearly impervious to physical blades.

items.name: Gillian's Keepsake Ring
items.specs: Keepsake Brass Band (+1 Charisma, Morale Anchor, Sentiment Relic).
items.notes: A polished brass ring engraved with initials, clutched obsessively by Farnham the Drunk. It is the sole memento of his life before Archbishop Lazarus led Tristram's men into the Butcher's ambush, anchoring his shattered sanity.

items.name: Naj's Puzzler Teleportation Staff
items.specs: Elderwood Teleportation Staff (60 Charges of Phase Shift, +1 All Sorcerer Skills).
items.notes: A twisted elderwood staff crowned with an unblinking amber eye, carried by Adria the Witch outside her swamp shanty. Allows instantaneous spatial teleportation through solid dungeon masonry, bypassing demonic chokeholds.

items.name: Staff of the Horadric Brotherhood
items.specs: Elder Horadric Walking Staff (Dispels Illusions, Decodes Ancient Dialects).
items.notes: A weathered ash-wood staff carved with intricate Horadric runes by Deckard Cain's ancestor Jered Cain. Cain leans upon it while seated beside the Tristram well, using its focusing jewel to identify unknown artifacts.

items.name: Farnham's Silver Whiskey Flask
items.specs: Dented Pewter Liquor Flask (Tempers Morale Panics, Fortifies Pain Resistance).
items.notes: A heavily dented pewter flask filled with foul, fiery grain liquor. Farnham drinks from it continuously to drown out the screams of Tristram's butchered boys that echo endlessly inside his head.

items.name: Pepin's Concentrated Healing Elixirs
items.specs: Concentrated Potion Satchel (Restores 100% Health, Purifies Poisons).
items.notes: A leather satchel containing thick crimson elixirs brewed by Pepin using distilled herbs, honey, and blessed water. A single swallow instantly knits torn muscle and halts demonic festering.

items.name: Tome of Town Portal Mastery
items.specs: Bound Grimoire (Contains 20 Spatial Town Portal Runes).
items.notes: A parchment codex bound in treated sheepskin, inscribed by Adria with spatial relocation coordinates. Tearing a leaf tears open a swirling blue dimensional rift connecting the deepest hells directly to Tristram's town square.

items.name: Crystalline Shard of the Worldstone
items.specs: Primordial Crystal Shard (Vibrates with Creation Magic, Reshapes Reality).
items.notes: A translucent, humming crystal fragment carried by Inarius the Veiled Prophet. It resonates with the primordial song of the Worldstone that cloaked Sanctuary from Heaven and Hell, bending spatial laws around its carrier.

items.name: Lilith's Blood Petal Talisman
items.specs: Carved Obsidian Talisman (Drains Blood to Unleash Demonic Metamorphosis).
items.notes: A black obsidian talisman shaped like an unfolding blood-rose, carried by Lilith, Mother of Sanctuary. When dipped in human blood, it awakens dormant Nephalem bloodlines, granting terrifying demonic strength at the expense of human empathy.

items.name: Uldyssian's Nephalem Focus
items.specs: Farmer's Rough Whetstone (Focuses Latent Nephalem God-Magic).
items.notes: An ordinary-looking stone whetstone carried by Uldyssian ul-Diomed during his days as a simple farmer in Seram. Under high stress, his dormant Nephalem power surged through it, transforming simple stone into an unbreakable divine conduit.

items.name: El'druin, the Sword of Justice (Hilt)
items.specs: Celestial Sword Hilt (Passes Harmlessly Through the Just, Cuts Evil Unopposed).
items.notes: The glowing platinum hilt of El'druin, the Sword of Justice, wielded by the Archangel Tyrael. Forged in the heart of the Crystal Arch, its blade passes harmlessly through righteous mortals while vaporizing demons into celestial ash.

items.name: Amber Soulstone Binding Shards
items.specs: Horadric Binding Matrix (Designed to Entomb the Prime Evil Baal).
items.notes: A shattered amber crystal lattice crafted by Tal Rasha and Jered Cain. Its containment matrix was intended to hold Baal, Lord of Destruction, until the golden crystal shattered during the desert confrontation.

items.name: Queen Asylla's Royal Signet
items.specs: Beheaded Queen's Gold Signet (Royal Seal of Khanduras, Bleeds When Evil is Near).
items.notes: A heavy gold signet ring bearing the crest of the Kingdom of Khanduras, worn by Queen Asylla before her mad husband King Leoric ordered her beheading on the guillotine. The ring weeps cold blood whenever demons approach.

items.name: Prince Albrecht's Wooden Toy Sword
items.specs: Child's Toy Sword (Carved Pine, Triggers Remorse in Albrecht's Vessel).
items.notes: A small toy sword carved from fragrant pine, dropped by little Prince Albrecht when Archbishop Lazarus abducted him from the palace bedrooms. Showing the toy to the demonic vessel of Diablo causes the beast to hesitate as the child's soul struggles beneath the surface.

items.name: Rathma's Carved Dragonbone Dagger
items.specs: Ancient Dragonbone Kris (Maintains the Great Balance, Summons Bone Spikes).
items.notes: An ancient ceremonial kris carved from a rib of the Great Dragon Trag'Oul, wielded by Rathma (Linarian), the first Necromancer. It balances life and death, preventing the chaotic influence of Heaven or Hell from overtaking Sanctuary.

creatures.name: The Hidden
creatures.summary: An assortment of horrid demons that vanish and reappear a moment before attacking. Smart, quick and aggressive, many with ranged attacks; the tougher the version, the less time there is to react. Variants include the Hidden Demon, Stalker Demon, Unseen Demon and Illusion Weaver.

senses.blindspots: Drawn out of invisibility one or two at a time by short erratic zig-zag bursts with pauses; random swinging at them is ineffective.

anatomicalWeakSpots: They are vulnerable in the moment before they materialize, when a bow can kill them.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Adaptive Instinct (C:2)

spoorAndSigns: Casts spells that do not dissipate over distance, mostly lightning, with Fireball and Elemental also useful.
Carries a staff reserved for huge hordes.
vernacularFolklore: Called the 'pivot point' of Diablo in regard to a character's abilities.
In a manner of speaking the Sorcerer can emulate a Warrior or Rogue.

creatures.name: Undead
creatures.subtype: Putrefying dead (Skeletons, Zombies, Ghouls, Rotting Corpses)
creatures.summary: The class of putrefying creatures including Skeletons, Zombies, Ghouls, Rotting Corpses and their kin. The abhorred are best met with Holy Bolt or Fire Magic, and otherwise with attacks tailored to each kind.

senses.blindspots: Little sign of tactics or guile; they press forward on instinct.

anatomicalWeakSpots: Each kind has its own best way to be fought, so attacks should be tailored to the template.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Local Grazer or Scavenger (E:2), Rigid Scripted Instinct (C:3)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Travelers avoid crypts and graveyard approaches or hire armed escorts, and lone wanderers take the long way around.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Attack the nearest living target and continue until it stops moving.

cues.label: Living creature within reach?
Living creature in sight?

signatureActions.name: Relentless advance
signatureActions.trigger: A living intruder enters their halls
signatureActions.effect: The putrefying dead press in and attack in numbers, with no sign of fear.

instinctiveQuirks: Called the abhorred, they inspire revulsion in the living.
spoorAndSigns: Rot-stench
Scattered bones
Disturbed graves
vernacularFolklore: Holy Bolt and Fire Magic are the favored answers to the abhorred.

creatures.name: Undead Zombie Family
creatures.subtype: Slow Undead (Zombie, Ghoul, Rotting Carcass, Black Death)
creatures.summary: Slow, deliberate Undead including the Zombie, Ghoul, Rotting Carcass and Black Death, all immune to magic. The tougher versions inflict serious damage, especially when they swarm, but their slowness lets targets be picked off one at a time.

senses.blindspots: Slow and deliberate, easily kited.

anatomicalWeakSpots: Their slowness lets attackers pick targets one at a time and keep them from swarming.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Local Grazer or Scavenger (E:2), Rigid Scripted Instinct (C:3)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Swarms of the tougher kinds hold crypts and passages against casual travelers, and parties hire guards for the way through.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Press the nearest living target until it falls or escapes.

cues.label: Living target adjacent?
Others of its kind nearby?

signatureActions.name: Swarm
signatureActions.effect: Together even slow zombies inflict serious damage.

signatureActions.name: Heavy blow
signatureActions.trigger: A target within reach of the tougher kinds
signatureActions.effect: A slow but punishing strike.

instinctiveQuirks: Slow and deliberate.
spoorAndSigns: Rot-stench
Dragging tracks
vernacularFolklore: Don't let them swarm.

creatures.name: Warrior
creatures.summary: The strongest and toughest class, excelling in hand-to-hand combat with heavy armor and massive weapons. He is a skillful craftsman who can repair weapons and armor in the field, though no match for a true blacksmith. He comes into his prime midway through the game.

senses.blindspots: Distant magical attackers; without magical resistance the bottom-dwellers have their way with him from afar.

anatomicalWeakSpots: Without raised magical resistances, crowds of magical monsters at the bottom of the dungeon drain his health quickly.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Fighter (S:3), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Adaptive Instinct (C:2)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Warriors with good armor and a vicious weapon can stand and fight demons, so travelers hire them as guards for dangerous routes.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Stop at the first cue: if the enemy is in reach, strike; if gear is damaged, repair it.

cues.label: Is gear damaged and no true smith near?
Is the enemy a distant magic user without resistance?

signatureActions.name: Field repair
signatureActions.effect: Repairs them in the field; skill grows with experience.

signatureActions.name: Heavy axe chop
signatureActions.effect: A large axe and an attitude deal effectively with them.

signatureActions.name: Fast-hit magic axe
signatureActions.effect: A magic axe with a fast hit or fast recovery makes a lethal combination.

instinctiveQuirks: Uses many Health Scrolls and Potions at the beginning of the game.
Prefers repairing items himself rather than paying, unless irreplaceable.
Takes a shield early, an axe mid-game, a shield again late.
spoorAndSigns: Heavy armor and cumbrous axes, weighty clubs and massive blades.
vernacularFolklore: Master of hand-to-hand combat.
Only the bravest Warrior, with a vicious weapon in hand, can go toe to toe with one.

harvestYields.component: Field repair of weapons and armor
